Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family holiday is approaching, which is a traditional time for everyone to reconnect.
Expectation2: Ensure client satisfaction and address any concerns or complaints professionally
Situation2: An easygoing regular politely asks for a tiny adjustment to their fringe.
Story: The salon was buzzing with the usual pre-holiday excitement, and I was finishing up a trim for Mrs. Lee, one of my favorite regulars. She smiled at her reflection, then hesitated, gently touching her fringe. “Could you just take a little more off here?” she asked, her tone apologetic. I nodded, reaching for my scissors, but my phone vibrated in my pocket for the third time in ten minutes. I knew it was my daughter, probably about the family holiday dinner this weekend. Every year, I’m the one who calls around, makes sure everyone’s coming, and keeps the tradition alive. I could almost hear my grandson’s voice, asking if I’d bring my famous cookies. But right now, Mrs. Lee was waiting, trusting me to get her hair just right before her own family gathering. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in—my family expecting my warmth and attention, my client expecting my focus and skill. My hands hovered, scissors poised, as my heart tugged in two directions, unsure which role needed me more in this moment.
